geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the generic bent bar with a section-aware hall-like dominant mass so the section can support a clearer ground/public relationship.
Use a folded section to create a more legible massing response without turning the building into a tower or pure sculpture.
Preserve a broad, low-rise horizontal reading that better suits neighborhood-living than a vertical typology.
Add an explicit courtyard cut so the frontage can register as public rather than sealed.
Keep the court substantial enough to be read in plan and section.
Orient the carved public void to the verified access side.
Make the new public void the organizing root while keeping the hall in its ancestry so the dominant mass remains intact.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the primary mass from a generic courtyard placeholder into an explicit carved ground void so the access edge can read as a public threshold.
Keep the void modest and usable rather than over-eroding the dominant mass.
Align the public opening to the program's required access side so the ground edge becomes legible.
Strengthen the section continuity between the carved ground condition and upper mass so the program reads as one spatial rule.
Reinforce the frontage-facing terrace logic to activate the access edge.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass across all four views, so it avoids the severe failure of incoherence or view-dependent collision. The silhouette is basically a single bent/prismatic volume with a mild top articulation rather than a meaningless stack, which suits the neighborhood-living brief better than a sculptural object. However, the public-void logic is weak: the blue access edge is not met with a clearly carved court, seam, or undercut, so the street threshold remains only partially expressed. The form also feels somewhat generic-boxy in section, with limited evidence of the active ground/public sequence the program wants. Still, the mass is repairably consistent and the dominant gesture survives as a compact prismatic/bar-like object with modest profile variation, so it passes the hard program gate.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller, more tower-like and more urban-monumental than this compact neighborhood building; use as a continuity/clarity reference, not as a height model.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single legible dominant mass with a tapered/stepped profile can still read as a coherent mixed-use object when the silhouette is continuous and not over-fragmented.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology; the candidate should stay low-rise/mixed-use and should not copy the tower condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clean dominant vertical mass with a subtle section inflection can preserve hierarchy while varying the upper silhouette.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a small cafe/restaurant and is much more horizontal; its active threshold is the transferable part, not the overall form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact commercial mass can gain program legibility through a simple ground-edge response and a controlled upper volume.

warnings: Access edge response is underdeveloped relative to the verified frontage.
Public void/court is too implicit; the ground condition could be more legible.
The silhouette is coherent but still close to a generic compact box-bar; a stronger carved threshold would improve program fit.
